# PR #1788: Patch: the AI weighs an even trade or a trade up beside its free kills, ahead of its plays

Closes #1779

The AI now tries even trades and trade-ups early in its turn instead of last. Each attacker's best kill at an even trade or better gets its own tier in the move order, after the winning trades and before the plays. A trade counts as even or better when the opponent model's own read (`reply.rs`'s `trade_value`) puts it at 0 or more. The gate passes. The improve-dev screen against the parent came out neutral, 199–201, and the change ships under the plan's rule for a neutral screen.

## What changed

- **`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`**: `trade_value` is now `pub(crate)` and returns `Trade { value, kills }` instead of a bare `f64`. `ranked_attacks` reads `.value`, so the opponent's reply behaves exactly as before.

  - New `even_trade`: it returns the trade's value when the attack kills its target and the value is at least 0.
  - `in_move_order` tags every tier-4 attack with that value. For each attacker, the best one (ties: the first) moves into the new bucket, which keeps `legal_actions` order.

# #1779: Patch: the AI weighs an even trade or a trade up beside its free kills, ahead of its plays
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
When the AI orders the moves it will try on its turn, it splits attacks into two piles: kills where its attacker survives, which it tries early, and everything else, which it tries last, beside attacks that just throw a unit away. An even trade (my 3/3 for your 3/3), a trade up (my 1-mana poisonous unit for your 9/9) and any kill that costs the attacker its life all sit in that last pile, and on a busy turn they are cut before the AI looks at them. So the AI can spend a removal spell on a big Taunt it could have killed with a 1-mana poisonous unit. Its model of the human already makes these trades. Once built, its own turn considers them early too.

## Why
- The move order is "hero attacks, winning trades, plays round-robin, answers, other attacks" (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`, around 590, `in_move_order`). The cut keeps 20 moves at the root and 6 deeper (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:40-41`, `crates/ai/src/search.rs:111`).
- Tier 1 is only `kills_and_survives` (`candidates.rs`, around 243-294). `attack_tier` (around 296-308) gives every other attack on a unit tier 4, the tier of a suicide attack. A Poisonous kill whose attacker dies to the strike back ends `taken < a.health`, false, so it lands in tier 4.
- The AI's opponent model already prices these attacks. `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`'s `trade_value` (around 64-110) values a kill at the target's `unit_worth` less the attacker's when it dies, and its static trader takes "a kill it survives, a trade up" (`reply.rs:14-15`).
- Wrong-House Attacker (`classicplus-006`, a 1/1 with Rush, Lifesteal and Poisonous, whose worth is that trade up) reads 0.5203 on the AI's dealt-deck measure (`DEALT_Q`, `crates/ai/src/shadow_ban.rs`), 10th lowest of 261.

## Proposal
- Add a tier between the winning trades and the plays: an attack that kills its target and whose `trade_value` is at least 0, an even trade or better. Make `trade_value` `pub(crate)` and reuse it rather than copying it.
- Attacks that kill nothing stay where they are.
- To leave room for plays in the deeper steps' 6 slots, only each attacker's best such attack enters the tier; the rest stay in tier 4.

## Where it lands
- `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs` (`attack_tier`, `in_move_order`), and `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` (visibility only)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs`, or a scenario test beside it
- `crates/ai/README.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a play of Wrong-House Attacker into a lane facing a 9/9 Taunt, `expansion` at `AI_BUDGET.branching` holds its attack on the Taunt.
- [ ] On a hand that fills the root, `decide`'s line holds that trade rather than a removal spell on the Taunt.
- [ ] B18's P7 ("Mr. Vanilla does not throw itself into the 7/7 with armor 7") and every other puzzle still hold, and a losing trade stays in tier 4.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` passes, and the pull request reports an improve-dev screen against the parent and `stats` before and after for `classicplus-006`.

## Size and risks
Hard, since it is the AI, but small: about 25 lines and about 100 lines of tests. More attacks early in a line leave fewer slots for plays deeper in it, so it stands or falls on the screen. It edits `in_move_order`, like #1759 (in flight) and the X-card suggestion beside this one, so build them one after another.

## What it actually means
When the AI orders the moves it will try on its turn, it splits attacks into two piles: kills where its attacker survives, which it tries early, and everything else, which it tries last, beside attacks that just throw a unit away. An even trade (my 3/3 for your 3/3), a trade up (my 1-mana poisonous unit for your 9/9) and any kill that costs the attacker its life all sit in that last pile, and on a busy turn they are cut before the AI looks at them. So the AI can spend a removal spell on a big Taunt it could have killed with a 1-mana poisonous unit. Its model of the human already makes these trades. Once built, its own turn considers them early too.

## Why
- The move order is "hero attacks, winning trades, plays round-robin, answers, other attacks" (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`, around 590, `in_move_order`). The cut keeps 20 moves at the root and 6 deeper (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:40-41`, `crates/ai/src/search.rs:111`).
